AI is rapidly rewriting the process and paperwork layer for Orthoptists, but on-site judgment and professional experience still rest with people. This article breaks down the specific impact and how to respond.

It does not suit impatient people who dislike complications and communicate poorly. Examinations and training depend on cooperation; when a child does not cooperate, the method must be adjusted repeatedly without rushing.

A common path is: optometry, clinical medicine, or nursing program -> internship at an ophthalmology hospital or optometry center -> shadow strabismus and binocular vision examinations -> obtain optometry or related professional credentials -> independently conduct orthoptic examinations and develop training plans.

This career suits attentive, patient people who communicate well with children. Strabismus examinations often require calming a crying child within minutes. People who can settle the child while exercising professional judgment are best suited.

Orthoptists work under ophthalmologists to examine and assess binocular vision disorders such as strabismus, amblyopia, and diplopia, deliver vision therapy and corrective plans, and continuously track and record outcomes throughout treatment.

paragraphs: For a child's initial strabismus visit, first review the history and previous records, then use an occluder and prisms to measure alignment. Have the child follow a light to observe eye movement, recording the angle of deviation and stereopsis. Afterward, organize the data for the physician, discuss whether to begin with occlusion or proceed directly to surgery, and explain the training schedule to the parents. A day in the examination room is filled with children reluctant to cooperate, demanding patience and skill.

Data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) show that in 2024, about 41,300 orthoptists were employed. By 2034, employment is projected to reach 42,200, a net increase of about 900 jobs, with about 2,400 openings per year. In 2026, the median annual salary is about $113,700 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace orthoptists, but it will accelerate examination and analysis. Automated eye-position tracking, image analysis, and data reports let orthoptists shift time from organizing data to conducting examinations, designing plans, and communicating with parents. The truly scarce skill is gaining cooperation from children and parents and sustaining adherence to the plan.

Opticians address seeing clearly through refraction and eyewear; orthoptists address aligning vision through treatment of binocular vision problems such as strabismus, amblyopia, and diplopia. The former focuses on refractive correction, while the latter focuses on visual function examinations and rehabilitation.

subject.name: Orthoptists
subject.summary: Orthoptists help both eyes align to see. They examine, assess, and provide therapeutic training for eye-alignment and binocular vision problems such as strabismus, amblyopia, and diplopia, serving as specialized members of the ophthalmic care chain.
